title: Be My Multiple, I'll Be Your Factor

concepts.name: Factors
concepts.description: Factors are numbers that divide another number exactly without leaving a remainder. Students explore factors using arrays, multiplication tables, and division.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify all the factors of a given whole number.

concepts.name: Multiples
concepts.description: Multiples are obtained by multiplying a number by whole numbers. Students observe that every number has infinitely many multiples.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to generate multiples of a given number.

concepts.name: Relationship Between Factors and Multiples
concepts.description: Factors and multiples are closely related through multiplication and division. Understanding this relationship helps solve number problems efficiently.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain the relationship between factors and multiples using examples.

concepts.name: Rules of Divisibility
concepts.description: Divisibility rules provide quick methods to determine whether a number is divisible by another without performing long division.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to apply divisibility rules for 2, 3, 5, 9, and 10.

concepts.name: Testing Divisibility
concepts.description: Students use divisibility rules to identify factors and simplify calculations involving large numbers.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to determine whether a given number is divisible by another using appropriate divisibility rules.

concepts.name: Prime Numbers
concepts.description: Prime numbers have exactly two distinct factors: 1 and the number itself. They serve as the building blocks of whole numbers.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify prime numbers within a given range.

concepts.name: Composite Numbers
concepts.description: Composite numbers have more than two factors and can be expressed as the product of smaller whole numbers.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to distinguish composite numbers from prime numbers.

concepts.name: Special Numbers
concepts.description: The number 1 is neither prime nor composite because it has only one factor. Students learn to classify numbers correctly.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to classify numbers as prime, composite, or neither.

concepts.name: Common Factors
concepts.description: Common factors are numbers that divide two or more numbers exactly. Identifying common factors helps compare and simplify numerical relationships.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to determine the common factors of two or more numbers.

concepts.name: Common Multiples
concepts.description: Common multiples are numbers that appear in the multiplication tables of two or more numbers. They are useful in solving problems involving repeated events.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify common multiples of two or more numbers.

concepts.name: Applications of Factors and Multiples
concepts.description: Factors and multiples are applied in grouping objects, arranging items equally, scheduling repeated events, and solving everyday mathematical problems.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to solve real-life problems involving factors and multiples.

concepts.name: Understanding Factors and Multiples
concepts.description: This chapter develops number sense by exploring factors, multiples, divisibility rules, prime and composite numbers, and common factors and multiples through practical activities.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify, compare, and apply factors and multiples to solve mathematical and real-life problems.
